prompt: Assess this claim: black people are underrepresented in university leadership.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is plausible, but it needs a country, timeframe, and definition of “university leadership” to assess accurately. That could mean university presidents, governing boards, deans, or department heads—and representation can differ across those roles.

“Underrepresented” also needs a benchmark: the Black share of leadership compared with the Black share of the national population, students, academic staff, or people eligible for those positions. Each comparison answers a different question.

A defensible version would be: “In [country/year], Black people held X% of [specified leadership roles], compared with Y% of [specified comparison group].” Without those details and supporting data, the claim is too broad to confirm. A measured disparity would establish underrepresentation relative to that benchmark; it would not, by itself, establish its causes.
